findings: macOS systemMemory estimates available pages as free_count plus0.75*inactive_count. Source explicitly calls this a guess; it is not a process allocation reservation or memory-pressure guarantee. Earlier pooled allocator advisory limit should be described accordingly.
macOS memoryUsage always returns two zero values. Zero observations cannot be interpreted as measured zero resident/virtual memory; no actual host memory benchmark run.

Linux systemMemory uses MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo and initializes values to0 on open failure. It parses each line numeric token without shape/conversion validation. No cgroup/process quota integration visible in this helper.

Linux memoryUsage tokenizes /proc/self/stat by whitespace, including comm field, and does not check stream extraction success; vsize/rss are uninitialized before extraction. Names containing spaces or failed reads require separate handling. No process mutation, invalid-read or sanitizer test run.

Windows systemMemory initializes0 on GlobalMemoryStatusEx failure; memoryUsage similarly initializes0 on failure. API success not exposed in return type, so unknown and genuine zero are conflated to caller.

Env setIdleProcessPriority changes scheduling only; no proof of bounded CPU/memory or cancellation responsiveness. Platform-specific allocator size macros have different underlying APIs; cross-platform byte counts not qualified here.
